prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, from heterobifunctional PROTACs to the cereblon-mediated mechanism of molecular glue degraders

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from proton-coupled electron transfer (B025) to targeted protein degradation (B063), credited to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The first-round exchange showed me that this candidate has a definable core achievement, which I said in round 1 was my condition for supporting it. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the heterobifunctional PROTAC (2001 onward), which is a chemist's design of a molecule that induces proximity between an E3 ligase and a chosen protein. Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which supplied the molecular mechanism of glue degraders. Linke's division of credit into a concept strand and a mechanism strand yields a principled three-person set that three members arrived at independently. The chemistry is explicit (ligand and linker design, ternary-complex cooperativity, catalytic turnover of the target), and the mechanism has been reproduced across many laboratories. As a biochemist I also value that it gives an acute, reversible way to remove a protein, which changes how mechanism can be tested. I am treating this as a judgment on originality and mechanistic content, and I do not count the number of members who rank it.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so the therapeutic validation is still prospective, and I remain uneasy about acting before it exists. Attribution is exclusionary: Ciulli's VHL ligands made PROTACs drug-like, and Ito (cereblon co-discoverer), Gray, Sakamoto and Kim each have real claims. The citation also joins two historically distinct strands, which Somfai and Aili both noted. I accept that a mechanism-centred wording only partly answers this. Proton-coupled electron transfer remains, in my own judgment, the more fundamental piece of chemistry, and moving away from it is a concession to the lack of a single sharply defined achievement and to attribution that four strong claimants make hard to resolve. It is not a change of view about its science.

responses.point: Chabes asked whether I could support B063 if B025 does not gain traction, and noted that PCET support is narrow and that its attribution is open.
responses.response: Yes, and after this round I do. His point that PROTAC conception and the cereblon mechanism can be cited together, with priority not contested in the primary papers, is better than anything I could say for dividing PCET credit among Mayer, Hammes-Schiffer, Nocera and Meyer. I still hold that the maturity concern counts against timing, and I would want the citation to state the achievement as a design principle and a mechanism, not as clinical success.

responses.point: Linke asked whether I could narrow B025 to a single sharply defined achievement, and he handled B063 by crediting the concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the cereblon mechanism (Handa) and leaving out VHL chemistry.
responses.response: I could not narrow it convincingly. PCET is a framework built by experiment and theory over three decades, and any citation would either be very broad or exclude Meyer, whose claim is foundational. That is a fair objection and it carries weight with me. Your split for B063 is the clearer one, and I agree that Deshaies should stay, since the 2001 paper was joint work. Where I differ is that I would not describe the absence of an approval as a footnote, and I take your own caution on that point seriously.

responses.point: Zou ranked zeolite design above PCET because PCET is mostly an explanatory framework, whereas molecular-sieve design is both concept and large-scale technology, and he regards the PCET attribution as hard with Meyer's early work foundational.
responses.response: The distinction between explanatory and enabling is a fair one, and it is part of why I no longer put B025 first. I do not agree that explanatory impact is lesser, since PCET changed how enzyme mechanisms are formulated. For this year, though, I would put a new modality with an explicit design principle ahead of B051, in part because the porous-materials area was addressed so recently by the 2025 prize and in part because of attribution among five candidates. I also note that you and I are Stockholm University colleagues, which does not affect either judgment.

responses.point: Aili would put Handa ahead of Ciulli in a three-person cut, and concedes that timing is the main reservation.
responses.response: I agree with him on Handa. Without the cereblon mechanism the glue half of the field has no explanation, and the Handa work is not a later optimisation of what Crews and Deshaies did. I accept Ciulli's role in making PROTACs drug-like, but that is a refinement of a concept already demonstrated, and I would leave it to the citation's wording and the committee's record to say so. On timing I am less comfortable than he is, and I would want the committee to say explicitly why it acts before approval.

responses.point: Aqvist pairs ionizable lipid nanoparticles (Cullis, Anderson) with base editing (Liu) as a two-part prize and does not think a three-person lipid part leaves room for a second achievement.
responses.response: I take his point on maturity, which is the strongest argument for B035 over B063, and I list B035 as an alternative for that reason. I would not support a two-part prize here. The two parts rest on attribution that I regard as less settled than for B063, with the patent entanglement in lipid delivery and with Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo left out of a Liu-only base-editing citation. I also share his and Sparr's doubt about whether delivery technology counts as chemistry after the 2023 Medicine prize.

uncertainties: Whether the committee is willing to act before the first degrader approval, and if not, what evidence would suffice.
Whether Ciulli or Ito should displace Deshaies or Handa, and whether the citation wording can acknowledge the VHL and cereblon co-discovery strands without a fourth name.
Whether PCET (B025) is held back by attribution among Mayer, Hammes-Schiffer, Nocera and Meyer or by it being a field and not a discovery; I may be underrating a fair route to a defined citation.
Whether ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B035) would be a better choice than B063 if the committee weights maturity above conceptual novelty and settles the Vancouver and lipidoid attribution.
statement.conflict_note: I have no tie to any credited person on the shortlist. My research on proton transfer in respiratory enzymes is scientifically close to B025, which I preferred in round 1 and now list as an alternative. I withdrew support for it as first choice and ask colleagues to treat my earlier enthusiasm for it as a possible bias. I have no scientific proximity to B063. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, who prefers B051; this does not bear on any candidate. I see no need for recusal.
